source.work: MongoDB Manual (Cursors: limit and batch size)
source.paraphrase: A find without limit returns every matching document. Cap the result with limit() before materializing it.

invariants.why: An unbounded find streams the whole match set into memory, so one request can exhaust the server and the client.
invariants.fixHint: Chain .limit(n) in the same statement as .find(), or use a paginated query with an explicit page size.
invariants.avoid: Sorting without a limit only orders the rows; it does not bound them. findOne() is already bounded and needs no limit.

source.paraphrase: $where runs JavaScript per document and $expr evaluates an expression tree. Neither should be built from request input.

invariants.why: Request-controlled expressions escape field comparison and run attacker-shaped logic inside the query.
invariants.fixHint: Compare request values against named fields with plain equality, and allowlist any operator the client may choose.
invariants.avoid: $expr with $eq looks declarative but still evaluates request input. Plain field equality with request values stays allowed.

source.paraphrase: The ObjectId constructor throws on values that are not 12 bytes or 24 hex characters. Validate with ObjectId.isValid() first.

invariants.why: Building an ObjectId straight from request input turns garbage ids into unhandled throws instead of 400s.
invariants.fixHint: Copy the input to a local, reject it when ObjectId.isValid() is false, then construct the ObjectId from the local.
invariants.avoid: Bracket access (req.query["id"]) reads the same request input and throws the same way. Validating the local covers both.

source.paraphrase: $where, $function, and $accumulator execute JavaScript on the server for the documents they visit.

invariants.why: Server-side JavaScript in a pipeline runs per document with the server's privileges and defeats operator-level optimization.
invariants.fixHint: Rewrite the stage with declarative operators ($match, $group, $project, $addFields) instead of embedded functions.
invariants.avoid: $function nested inside $project is the same server-side JavaScript, not a safe projection.

source.work: MongoDB Manual (db.collection.updateOne and updateMany) and MongoDB Node.js driver
source.locator: update parameter: update operator expressions or an aggregation pipeline; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.updateOne/
source.paraphrase: The update argument holds only update operator expressions such as $set, or an aggregation pipeline. Replacing the whole document is replaceOne's job. The Node.js driver rejects an update document with no operators.

invariants.why: A plain field object passed as the update throws MongoInvalidArgumentError ("Update document requires atomic operators") on every call, so the write never happens.
invariants.fixHint: Wrap the fields in $set, or use another operator such as $inc or $unset. Use an update pipeline array for computed fields, and replaceOne to replace the whole document.
invariants.avoid: Model.collection is the raw driver collection; it skips Mongoose's automatic $set cast. Mongoose Model.updateOne(filter, { name }) passes because Mongoose adds $set. The rule reads driver receivers: .collection(...), .collection, or a const bound to .collection(...) in the same file. An update object built in a variable, or one starting with a spread, is not judged.

source.paraphrase: Passing an empty filter document {} to deleteMany matches and removes every document in the collection.

invariants.why: Calling collection.deleteMany({}) or Model.deleteMany() in application code drops every document in the collection in a single command.
invariants.fixHint: Pass a non-empty filter document such as { tenantId, expiredAt: { $lt: now } } to deleteMany.
invariants.avoid: Matches literal deleteMany() and deleteMany({}) calls (including with a second options argument). Dynamic filter variables are not evaluated.

relations.why: A bare .deleteMany() or .deleteMany({}) call has no where property and an empty filter, so both rules report it when both packs are active.
relations.settle: Keep both. Passing a non-empty filter (or a where clause in Prisma) satisfies both; disable the pack for the database you do not use in that module.
